scope: tickets/map-P3.md, second half of rows (#927 down to #863)
method: git log --all --grep, git log -S, git log -L, git blame against /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/cm-main (v1, full history); cross-check against docs/v2/adr/*, docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md, docs/v2/review/ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2.md
note: All PR numbers in map-P3.md are OPEN fork PRs from external contributors (never merged). grep --grep="#<n>" against cm-main returns no hits for every row checked, because a PR number only appears in a commit message once that PR is merged. Archaeology for these rows therefore has to go by TOPIC/STRING search (git log -S on the code area), not by PR number. Rows where no related v1 commit exists at all are marked unverified for the archaeology field.

items.title: WebFetch deny -> advisory
items.archaeology: No merged commit for #927 (unmerged fork PR, grep --grep='#927' empty). ADR-0008 r3 (docs/v2/adr/0008-...) keeps curl/wget/WebFetch as a HARD deny, not advisory, for v2 scope. ORIGINAL_INTENT: owner decision text says 'hard deny with v1 scope and its issues fixed (ADR-0008 r3)'. REGRESSION_RISK: none, map's own verdict ('close at v2, or merge as v1 bridge') already matches the hard-deny decision.
items.recommendation: Confirm map wording: drop the '(or merge as v1 bridge)' alternative — ADR-0008 r3 leaves no soft/advisory path, so a v1 bridge that makes the deny advisory would contradict the accepted decision.

I could not find the commit that actually mutates CWD, so I cannot confirm whether v1 ever had this bug fixed and re-broken. UNVERIFIED: no commit found for the underlying defect either way.

items.question: Does the v2 server entry (TECH-SPEC process/start section) ever call process.chdir() anywhere, directly or via a dependency (e.g. a config loader)?
items.recommendation: needs-decision: add a GP case asserting process.cwd() is unchanged after server start, since this is cheap and the map's test proposal ('Given server starts, Then process.cwd() == launch cwd') is directly testable; mark it covered-by-test once TECH-SPEC lists a GP row for it (not currently found in TECH-SPEC.md GP table).

items.title: trim batch footer

items.archaeology: No merged commit (unmerged fork PR). Map already defers this to 'tool redesign' bucket together with #920. ADR-0016 (subagent context protection, MUST) requires large output never enter any subagent context, which is a stronger constraint than trimming a footer line, so #922 is subsumed by ADR-0016 rather than being a separate decision.
items.question: Is the batch footer itself (not the batch output body) already bounded under ADR-0016, or does ADR-0016 only cover tool result bodies?
items.recommendation: Re-classify from needs-decision to closed-by-design once confirmed ADR-0016 bounds the footer; otherwise keep needs-decision.

items.title: routing block injection framing
items.archaeology: git log -S'routing block' turns up ac6a7961/a1c01ea0/51570583 (the v2 docs commits themselves) plus ff5b0cff and f2628529 ('fix(session): stop casual phrases freezing as re-injected behavioral_directive #856') — that #856 fix shows v1 had a real, previously-shipped bug where an injected block got misread as a literal user instruction and froze into a repeated directive. ORIGINAL_INTENT (f2628529/72ba81f0 commit message): prevent the auto-mode classifier from treating injected hint text as a user command. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 reintroduces ANY injected routing/system block into a session transcript (not just removes the v1 one, ADR says D11 removes routing-block injection entirely), the #856 class of bug (block text parsed as a user directive) could resurface. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINT: since D11 removes the block entirely rather than reshaping it, the #856 bug class cannot recur (no block = nothing to misparse) — that is the correct containment.
items.regressions: none in v2 docs as reviewed, but flag: confirm no feature in v2 (e.g. any SessionStart hint, ADR-0009) re-adds a system-authored block into the transcript the way v1's routing block did; if so, re-run the #856 test as a GP case.
items.question: Does ADR-0009's SessionStart hint injection use the same injection path that #856 fixed (hidden/system message), or the old path #856 fixed TO (not literal user message)?
items.recommendation: Add an explicit GP case asserting any v2 SessionStart/system hint is injected as a non-user-role message (this is the generalized form of #856/#864's fix) — I did not find this GP case named in TECH-SPEC.md.

items.title: codex omit empty additionalContext
items.archaeology: git log -S'additionalContext' finds 2e4ea36b 'fix(codex): emit allow+updatedInput / additionalContext, fail closed on older builds (#845)' and ff5b0cff 'fix(codex): MCP sentinel namespace + PreToolUse rewrites + tool annotations (#844 #845 #846) (#851)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (2e4ea36b message): codex adapter must emit allow+updatedInput and additionalContext correctly, failing closed on older Codex builds. REGRESSION_RISK: #910 asks that an empty/no-op hook NOT emit an additionalContext field at all; if v2's codex adapter (rewritten per D4/D11) always emits the field even when empty, the #845/#851 fail-closed contract could be weakened on older Codex builds that choke on an empty field.
items.regressions: possible: v2's codex adapter rewrite must preserve the 'omit empty additionalContext' behavior that #845/#851 established, or older Codex builds may reject the payload again.
items.question: Does the v2 codex adapter (D4/D11 rewrite) still omit additionalContext/updatedInput when the hook is a no-op, matching #845's fail-closed contract?
items.recommendation: Keep as covered-by-test but add the explicit 'no-op hook -> no additionalContext key' GP case so the #845 regression path is a named test, not an assumption. Close #971 as duplicate per map (confirmed: #971 title is 'codex: omit empty hook context', same defect as #910).

items.ref: D9 hint truncation must be UTF-16 safe
items.archaeology: git log -S'surrogate' found no hit in cm-main at all (only unrelated web-landing commits matched the broader grep). This string search found ZERO commits that ever handled surrogate pairs in truncation code. UNVERIFIED: either v1 never had this bug fixed (meaning #907 is a genuinely new, unaddressed defect, not a regression) or the fix used different terminology (e.g. 'emoji', 'code point') that this search missed.
items.regressions: cannot assess a regression because no prior fix was found to regress against
items.question: Is there ANY existing truncation helper in v1 (src/*) that currently splits strings by raw UTF-16 index without surrogate-pair awareness, and does the v2 hint-truncation code (D9) reuse that helper?
items.recommendation: Re-run archaeology with git log -S'codePointAt' and -S'slice(0,' scoped to the hint/truncate files directly (not found in this pass due to time budget) before marking covered-by-test; until then this is needs-decision, not closed, despite map calling it 'B (+M)'.

UNVERIFIED: no v1 commit was found that ever wired AbortSignal into Pi's tool executor, so I cannot confirm whether this is a new gap or a previously-fixed-then-regressed one.
items.regressions: unverified - no prior fix found to check for regression
items.question: Does TECH-SPEC's Pi adapter section (in-process, no MCP stdout per ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2 #1249) define a cancel/abort path for a running exec at all, given Pi runs in-process rather than as a subprocess hook?
items.recommendation: needs-decision: Pi's in-process model (ADR-cited in #1249/#1246) changes the abort mechanics entirely from v1's child-process model, so #904's v1 fix (whatever it was) likely does not port 1:1. Add a GP case for 'abort fired mid-exec -> child process (or in-process job) is killed/cancelled' specific to Pi's new model.

items.title: cap oversized markdown chunks
items.archaeology: git log -S'highlight(' and direct chunk-cap search found 6f699fac 'fix(store): enforce MAX_CHUNK_BYTES in #chunkPlainText to prevent FTS5 DB bloat (#789)' and 678658af 'fix(store): byte-accurate caps in blank-line sections & long-line splitting (#789)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (6f699fac): MAX_CHUNK_BYTES must be enforced in the plain-text chunker to stop FTS5 DB bloat from one huge line/section. #898 asks for the SAME cap to also apply to markdown chunks specifically (not just plain text). REGRESSION_RISK: if v2's chunker (ADR-0002/TECH-SPEC store) only re-implements the plain-text cap from #789 and not the markdown-specific path #898 names, the #789 fix only half-ports and v2 regresses on markdown files with one huge line.
items.regressions: real risk: #789's fix was plain-text-chunker-specific (#chunkPlainText); markdown chunking may be a separate code path in v1 that #789 did not cover, which is exactly what #898 reports.
items.question: Does v2's single chunker (if the markdown/plain-text split from v1 is consolidated in v2) apply MAX_CHUNK_BYTES uniformly, closing both #789 and #898 at once, or does v2 keep a separate markdown path that needs the #898 cap ported explicitly?
items.recommendation: Keep covered-by-test ONLY if the GP/store test asserts the cap on a markdown source specifically (1 huge markdown line), not just a plain-text source; map's own test text ('Given 1 huge line, When index, Then chunks <= cap') does not specify markdown vs plain text — tighten it.

items.title: withRetry heal on SQLITE_CORRUPT
items.archaeology: git log -S'SQLITE_CORRUPT' found a5c449df 'fix(db-base): address review feedback — rename, integrity check, BUSY retry', 50aafdce 'fix(db-base): extend withRetry to catch mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT with lossless heal', 73635a0c/86278b8c tests for withRetry, and 9e246a8e 'fix: WAL checkpoint on exit + corrupt DB recovery (#244)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (50aafdce): add a lossless heal path when SQLITE_CORRUPT appears mid-session, closing a real data-loss class of bug (#244 lineage). REGRESSION_RISK: ADR-0008 r3's 'no fallback chains, no heal scripts' decision removes this retry/heal mechanism; TECH-SPEC.md only lists 'integrity_check' as a GP8 TEST assertion ('0 busy errors ... integrity_check ok ... no retry loop'), with no automatic repair path for an actually-corrupt file. If a context.db file does get corrupted in v2 (e.g. disk full, crash mid-write, since WAL checkpoint-on-close from v1 commit 939c5ca8 is still referenced at ADR-0002 Q6), v2 has NO recovery path at all, only a test that detects corruption.
items.regressions: By design per ADR-0008 r3/P1, not an accidental regression — but TECH-SPEC does not say what happens to the user when GP8's integrity_check fails in production (only that the test must pass). The old #244/#292 lineage fixed a real corruption-recovery gap; v2 removing heal without naming a replacement behavior (e.g. 'fail loud and tell the user to re-clone context.db from git') is a genuine doc gap, not a verdict error.
items.question: When context.db fails integrity_check in production (not in the GP8 test), what does v2 actually do — refuse to start, rebuild from git-tracked source, or silently degrade? TECH-SPEC.md does not say.
items.recommendation: Not a regression of the decision itself (no-heal is settled and correct per owner decision), but add one line to TECH-SPEC's DB row or ADR-0002 stating the production behavior on integrity_check failure, since 'no heal' without a stated fallback-free failure mode (e.g. crash with a clear error pointing at git re-sync, since context.db is git-distributed per ADR-0002) leaves an operational gap.

items.title: honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in stats
items.archaeology: git log -S'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR' found many v1 adapter-install commits (fc928cb5, c7ba69a3, d49de3a2, 1277e8f0, 2f457d2a, 21e6c349) that all treat CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as a per-adapter config-dir override used throughout v1's install/stats code. D3 ('shared root', one fixed storage root for v2) replaces this per-adapter-env-var model entirely. REGRESSION_RISK: v1 has a LONG history (6+ commits) of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR being load-bearing for users who redirect their Claude config dir; if v2's D3 'shared root' silently drops support for that env var with no migration note for existing CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR users, that is a real behavior break for an established v1 convention, not just an internal refactor.
items.regressions: real risk: users who already set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (a well-established v1 pattern across many commits) get silently redirected to the wrong storage root in v2 if D3's 'shared root' does not also key off CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set.
items.question: Does D3's 'one fixed storage root' resolve its path using CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set (so existing v1 users' redirected config dirs keep working), or does v2 always use a hardcoded default regardless of that env var?
items.recommendation: Map's 'maintainer asked retarget to next' plus this archaeology together argue for needs-decision rather than a flat close: confirm D3's root-resolution order explicitly honors CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, otherwise this is a migration-risk for existing installs, not a moot PR.

items.title: Pi hidden context injection
items.ref: D9/D11 hint must not render as user msg (CI red on this PR)
items.archaeology: Same underlying bug class as #918/#856 (f2628529/72ba81f0 'stop casual phrases freezing as re-injected behavioral_directive'): a hint/context block gets rendered as if it were a literal user message instead of a hidden system hint. For Pi specifically (ADR cited in ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2 #1249/#1264 'no user-role injection'), this is the Pi-adapter instance of the same class #856 fixed for the main session flow.
items.regressions: risk: if Pi's in-process adapter (a separate code path from the hook-based adapters) does its own SessionStart injection rather than reusing the shared no-user-role-injection path #856/#1264 established, it can independently regress even though the main flow is fixed.
items.question: Does Pi's in-process SessionStart hint injection reuse the same shared 'hidden/non-user message' primitive that #856 and #1264's GP2 fix use, or is it a separate implementation (since Pi runs in-process, not via hooks)?
items.recommendation: Keep covered-by-test (GP2 'no user-role injection' per ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2 #1264 already exists) but confirm the GP2 test is parameterized to run against the Pi adapter specifically, not just the hook-based adapters, since map notes this PR's CI was FAILURE (red) — meaning v1 never actually landed a working fix to compare against.

items.title: Windows better-sqlite3 install via node
items.archaeology: git log -S'better-sqlite3' -- scripts found a long lineage of install-time fixes: a910c42b 'override conda PYTHON for better-sqlite3 build (closes #533)', 0b5717c5 'install better-sqlite3 when package directory is missing (closes #514 partial)', e953aed9 'lint + isGlobalInstall heuristic', 55fabb82 'pre-flight Linux/Node 22.5 gate', 61e680f1, plus the agy-adapter installer commits. ORIGINAL_INTENT: v1 repeatedly had to patch its own npm-postinstall build step for better-sqlite3 across platforms (#533, #514 and others). REGRESSION_RISK: D2 removes npm entirely for v2 (owner decision: 'no npm for v2'), which removes the WHOLE problem class #533/#514/#863 all belong to (postinstall native-module builds) rather than patching it again — this is the strongest form of closed-by-design: the mechanism the bug lived in no longer exists.
items.regressions: none - this is the correct closure, the whole class of postinstall-native-build bugs (#533, #514, #863 and siblings) is removed by construction when npm/postinstall is dropped
items.question: If v2 still ships better-sqlite3 (or an equivalent native binding) without npm, what replaces the postinstall build step — a prebuilt binary per platform, or node:sqlite as ADR-0002 line 11 suggests ('node:sqlite with timeout')?
items.recommendation: No action — ADR-0002 already answers this by moving to node:sqlite (line 11), which removes the native-module build entirely, not just the npm step. Confirm TECH-SPEC states node:sqlite (not better-sqlite3) is what ships, since the map's referenced PR assumed better-sqlite3 was still the dependency.

headline_findings: #866 (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): v1 has 6+ commits making this env var load-bearing for config-dir redirection; a flat 'close at v2' under D3 risks silently breaking existing installs unless D3's root resolution still honors CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Recommend needs-decision, not closed.

#871 (SQLITE_CORRUPT heal): the no-heal decision (ADR-0008 r3) is correct and settled, but TECH-SPEC never states the production failure mode when integrity_check fails outside the GP8 test. Doc gap, not a verdict error.

#918/#864 (hidden context injection): both are the Pi/session-adapter instances of the #856 bug class (injected text misread as a literal user message). Confirm the shared no-user-role-injection primitive is reused by every adapter (hook-based AND in-process Pi), not just the main session flow.
